report.source_text: Conjunctival secretions were sampled on admission for bacteriological analysis and cultured on blood agar. Direct examination showed numerous leukocytes and rare gram-negative bacilli (Figure 1C). Regular, grey, smooth colonies grew the next day. The oxidase test was positive for the 1-3 mm diameter, non-hemolytic colonies (Figure 1D&E), strongly suggesting that the isolated strain belonged to Pasteurella genus. The involvement of Pasteurella multocida was also strongly suggested here by mannitol fermentation (API-20E Array) (Figure 1F) and confirmed by MALDI TOF mass spectrometry.

report.source_text: Taking into account the animal contact and the short incubation period, suggesting the involvement of Pasteurella genus, an antibiotherapy associating amoxicillin 2 g tid and amoxicillin/clavulanate 2 g tid was administered intravenously, immediately after bacteriological sampling. No topical therapy was prescribed excepted for artificial tears. The outcome was favourable in the next three days (Figure 1G), allowing discharge of the patient with amoxicillin (2 g tid per os) alone once usual full sensitivity of Pasteurella multocida strain to amoxicillin was confirmed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old Caucasian male with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma on active chemotherapy (lenalidomide and CHOP) sustained a right eye injury from his dog's sneeze during the fifth day after his third chemotherapy round. Within 4 hours, he developed purulent conjunctivitis with chemosis, conjunctival hyperemia, and inflammatory peri-orbital edema with skin rupture and purulent encystment above and below the eye, accompanied by fever (39°C). He presented 33 hours post-injury unable to open his right eye. Physical examination confirmed purulent conjunctivitis with marked peri-orbital edema. Laboratory workup showed normal WBC count with lymphopenia (reflecting his immunocompromised state), negative blood cultures, and CT imaging negative for intra-orbital extension. Conjunctival secretions cultured on blood agar grew regular, grey, smooth, non-hemolytic colonies within 24 hours. Gram stain showed numerous leukocytes and rare gram-negative bacilli. The isolate tested positive on oxidase test, fermented mannitol on API-20E array, and was confirmed as Pasteurella multocida by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. The strain demonstrated full sensitivity to amoxicillin. Intravenous therapy with amoxicillin 2g three times daily and amoxicillin/clavulanate 2g three times daily was initiated immediately after bacteriological sampling. Clinical response was favorable over the next three days, allowing discharge on oral amoxicillin 2g three times daily.
